rule: The install exists and records its version + every file's hash.
Every installed file still matches its recorded hash.
The verifier's own manifest is complete: every rule has a check or is advisory.
if_not_why: — (this row is the reason the matrix cannot rot; the second clause is D6's shape in general: a row that carries no check must be labelled advisory, or it claims verification it does not perform)

rule: No file goblin-stack did not create has been overwritten.
if_not_why: Detects a file the installer recorded as pre-existing (a `refused` entry) that has since vanished, or that is listed as installed anyway. The second clause is an internal-consistency guard: with correct code a refused path is never written, so it fires only if the installer regresses. The negative control exercises the vanished branch.

rule: HANDOFF.md exists at the root.
The HANDOFF carries its five required sections.
check: for h in 'START HERE' 'STATE|STATUS' 'GATES?' 'NEXT STEPS|NEXT' 'NOT VERIFIED|UNVERIFIED|NOT PROVEN|UNPROVEN|PENDING[^.]*DEVICE TEST'; do grep -qiE "^#{2,3}[[:space:]]+[^[:alpha:]]*($h)\b" HANDOFF.md || { echo "missing section: $h"; exit 1; }; done
if_not_why: Partial: proves a heading exists whose first word names the slot, not that the section's content is complete. The slot may use the repo's own vocabulary (the model repo's `### NEXT` passes; `Status`, `Gate`, `Unverified`, `Pending <x> device test` are accepted); a heading that merely contains the word (`## BOARD STATE`) does not satisfy `State`.

rule: Every gate number is a measurement with a date, never a copy.
check: awk 'BEGIN{bad=0;n=0} tolower($0) ~ /^#{2,3}[[:space:]]+[^[:alpha:]]*gates?([^[:alpha:]]|$)/ {g=1;next} g && /^#{1,3}[[:space:]]/ {g=0} g && /(tsc|build|hex|safelist|[0-9]+\/[0-9]+)[^=]*=/ {n++; if ($0 !~ /measured [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}/) {print; bad=1}} END {if (n==0) {print "no gate line inside the Gates section"; bad=1} exit bad}' HANDOFF.md
if_not_why: Partial: proves every gate-bearing line inside the `Gates` section carries a date, not that the number was re-measured that day. Historical gate lines outside that section are exempt by design - PROJECT-PRACTICE section 1's stale-sentence rule requires them to be kept.

rule: A stale sentence is corrected in place with a dated parenthetical, never deleted.
if_not_why: Detecting a silent deletion needs semantic judgement; a diff heuristic (>=5 removed non-empty lines with no 'corrected' addition) is too noisy to gate on. goblin-verify --only HP-04 prints the heuristic as a warning only.

rule: The HANDOFF names the HEAD it describes.
if_not_why: Deviation from the design spec, with the reason: the spec's literal check is `grep -q "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" HANDOFF.md`, which can never pass - committing the HANDOFF moves HEAD, so the file can only name a commit that is now an ancestor. The mechanised form is therefore 'the HANDOFF names a commit that exists in this repo AND is an ancestor of HEAD', which still catches the defect it exists for (a review/handoff artifact that names no commit at all).

rule: The current round has a SPEC.
if_not_why: Skipped when class: D and disabled: [spec].

rule: The SPEC is committed, not left untracked.
Every AC: item is checkable without a human.
if_not_why: Partial: structural only - a checkable-looking bullet can still be unfalsifiable. The matcher is `AC[0-9]*:` because the shipped template writes `- AC1: ...`; the literal `/AC:/` only saw a bullet that spelled the label without a number.

rule: The gate set is declared, never inferred from the stack.
Every declared gate runs and exits 0.
The round reports one line of measured numbers.
A ratchet is declared with a ceiling.
The ratchet has not risen.
Asserting harnesses follow the house shape.
if_not_why: A declared harness_dir that is absent FAILS when the class scaffolds one (config `scaffold_checks: yes`, classes A and C); a class that ships no harness dir (B/D/E) SKIPs with a reason. Keying the skip off the path alone let one config line switch this row and HS-02 off. A report utility in the same dir is counted and reported separately rather than failing the run.

rule: A check green on both trees proves nothing - the REPLAY must show RED pre-change.
Source probes read text with comments blanked first.
if_not_why: Recognising 'this probe reads source text' is semantic; a grep for the blanking helper produces false FAILs on harnesses that do not probe source.

rule: Commits carry the owner identity, not an ambient one.
The commit message was written to a file, not passed with -m.
if_not_why: A backtick lost to command substitution leaves no trace a later check can read. Reported as a heuristic (unbalanced backticks in a body) only.

rule: Commit-as-you-go: the working tree is not carrying a dead run's work.
No model name is hardcoded in any reusable rule.
check: for d in skills manifest bin templates presets .goblin .hermes; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue; grep -rniE '(d[e]epseek|cl[a]ude|g[p]t-[0-9]|gr[o]k|g[e]mini|g[l]m-[0-9]|k[i]mi)[a-z0-9.:_-]*' "$d" && exit 1; done; exit 0
if_not_why: — (the pattern is written with character classes so this row cannot match itself; tests/t-verify-red.sh proves it still catches a real model name)

rule: The review lane is a different model family from the code lane.
if_not_why: goblin-stack cannot choose the fleet's models; today's map resolves both roles to the same family. Reported as ADV, never gated.

rule: Role-pinned fan-out goes through kanban, not a model-less subagent spawn.
if_not_why: It is a fleet-runtime property: no repo-local file can observe which tool created a worker. Enforced at board level, described in docs/INTEGRATION.md.

rule: The reviewed artifact is named by SHA, and that SHA exists.
The gate is chosen by the change, not the repo, and the tier's evidence exists.
A new head voids the verdict.
Never bypass what the forge enforces.
if_not_why: Needs the forge: GitHub's restrictions do not apply to admins, and a sole-admin repo has nobody the gate binds. Not observable from the repo.

rule: No required check that self-skips.
if_not_why: Heuristic: 'all steps guarded' is textual.

rule: Runtime data is not test fixture: a gate run must not write it.
Snapshot before, verify after.
A significant change updates the docs that teach it.
if_not_why: 'Significant' is a judgement; a diff-size heuristic fails on the cases that matter.

rule: System-level changes are recorded in the vault via the pkm profile.
if_not_why: Vault writes route through another profile by a stricter rule than goblin-stack may add; the repo can only state it.

rule: Every shipped skill has name + description frontmatter.
check: for f in .hermes/skills/*/SKILL.md; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; head -n 1 "$f" | grep -qx -- '---' || exit 1; awk 'NR==1{next} /^---/{exit} /^name:/{n=1} /^description:/{d=1} END{exit !(n&&d)}' "$f" || exit 1; done

rule: The installed skills match their recorded hashes (no drift).
A rule with no mechanism is labelled advisory, and the advisory count is reported.
No tenant-specific string inside a reusable rule.
check: for d in skills manifest bin templates presets .goblin .hermes; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue; grep -rniE --exclude=goblin.yaml '(h[a]rvey|tech-g[o]blin|/h[o]me/[a-z]+|g[o]blin-ui|op[e]n-door|sup[r]eme|bb[t]ech|c[l]v)' "$d" && exit 1; done; exit 0
if_not_why: — (the same directory list MD-01 uses: the rules an install actually writes live in `.goblin/` and `.hermes/`, not in the source layout. The one documented exception is `.goblin/goblin.yaml`, which holds `models_file:`/`practice:` - per-machine config, not a rule - and is excluded by name. The pattern is written with character classes so this row cannot match itself.)

rule: The default branch is declared, not assumed.
Every part the class requires is present, and every part it forbids is absent.
An archive: true project verifies GREEN without a HANDOFF or gates.
if_not_why: Falsifiable: FAILs when `archive:` is not `true`/`false`, and when the config's value disagrees with the one the install recorded in `.goblin/installed.json` (so the waiver cannot be flipped on by hand). It cannot observe the *effect* of the waiver on the other rows without re-entering the runner.

rule: The installer never writes outside its target.
A second install is a no-op, and an upgrade reports created/updated/unchanged.
Every target-scope check goes RED under its own violation.
if_not_why: — (the negative control the verifier re-runs)

rule: The repo is portable: no personal path in any reusable rule.
check: tests/run-tests.sh (the PT-01 body over the source tree, plus tests/)
